title: Translation without false confidence
goal: Use independent checks to identify meaning changes and unresolved ambiguity.
explanation: Back-translation can expose problems, but two fluent translations can share the same error. Choose a non-sensitive text with numbers, negation, dates and an idiom. A bilingual human or authoritative glossary remains necessary for high-stakes use. Do not approve a translation solely because it comes back sounding plausible.
sampleInput: Original: “Please do not ship before 6 November. Send 12 blue mugs, not 21. ‘Break a leg’ in the final line is a friendly wish, not an injury instruction.”
prompt: Translate the supplied message into a language you can responsibly review. Preserve the date, quantity, negation and colour. Explain the idiom separately. In a fresh chat, translate the result back to English and list any ambiguous phrases. Do not certify the translation.
workedExample: Check ledger: no shipment before 6 November; quantity 12; blue; exclusion of 21; idiom means good luck. If the return translation says “ship by 6 November,” it has reversed an operational constraint despite fluent wording.

steps.title: Mark invariants
steps.text: Write a checklist of date, quantity, negation, colour and idiom before translating.

steps.title: Create a translation
steps.text: Keep the source and target text unchanged for comparison.

steps.title: Use a fresh check
steps.text: Back-translate in a separate context; if possible use an independent service rather than the same model.

steps.title: Inspect each invariant
steps.text: Record pass, fail or unresolved. Consult a bilingual reader or authoritative glossary for disputed language.

steps.title: Prepare a safe handoff
steps.text: Mark unresolved wording and state “not approved for contractual or safety-critical use.”

checks: All five meaning constraints are checked individually rather than judged on fluency.
A changed before/by instruction is flagged as a material failure.
The report states the limits of back-translation and names unresolved review needs.
commonMistakes: Assuming two AI systems are independent evidence of correctness.
Using an unfamiliar language without a competent human review route.
offline: Use two English paraphrases and inspect whether they preserve the same constraints. Label this a meaning-preservation exercise, not a translation test.
reflection: What important error could a fluent back-translation still miss?

evidence.title: Keep the build
evidence.detail: Save your original input, exact prompt and resulting artifact. All five meaning constraints are checked individually rather than judged on fluency.

evidence.title: Show what you tested
evidence.detail: Record a pass/fail result and evidence for every check below. A changed before/by instruction is flagged as a material failure.

evidence.title: Explain a limitation
evidence.detail: Write what changed after one deliberate revision and name a remaining failure mode. Assuming two AI systems are independent evidence of correctness.
